name: Doublo HIFU
lead: Doublo is an intense focused ultrasound (IFUS, also called HIFU) device made by HIRONIC Co. of Seongnam, Korea, used for noninvasive skin tightening of the face and neck [1][2]. The goal is a firmer, lifted look along the jawline and lower face without surgery: ultrasound energy is focused to heat tissue beneath the skin surface, which is meant to prompt collagen remodelling and tightening [1][3].

A 2015 study by Suh and colleagues in the Journal of Cosmetic and Laser Therapy treated 11 patients with facial laxity (mean age 46, range 35-64) and took skin biopsies before treatment and two months afterwards. Blinded investigators rated photographic improvement, and the authors reported more collagen fibres in the lower dermis and between fat layers [1]. A 2020 prospective study by Friedman and colleagues, in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology, reported the authors' experience with the Doublo device in patients with neck and lower-face laxity, rated by two independent dermatologists [2].
Researchers describe IFUS as a nonablative technology with a good safety profile, noting that most clinical studies have examined a different system, the Ulthera device [2].

angle.text: Doublo treatments are used to tighten mild sagging along the jawline and neck without surgery. The 2015 study found more collagen on biopsy two months after treatment, and the 2020 study reported benefit for selected patients with minor sagging [1][2].

paras: Intense focused ultrasound produces thermal effects at various depths while sparing the overlying tissue, and is used for skin laxity [1]. The 2020 paper characterises it as a nonablative skin-tightening technology [2]. General background on focused ultrasound notes that the focal point is heated to roughly 65 to 85 degrees Celsius and that tissue held above 60 degrees for more than a second is irreversibly damaged, which is the basis of the thermal effect [3].

Focused ultrasound uses non-ionising sound at lower frequencies than diagnostic ultrasound, concentrated on a target typically 2-3 mm wide. Wikipedia states that tissue at the focus can reach 65 to 85 C and that cavitation can contribute mechanical effects [3]. Cosmetic systems apply this to the dermis and deeper layers rather than to tumours or tremor targets, which are the medical uses Wikipedia describes for HIFU, such as essential tremor, prostate and liver tumours and kidney stones [3]. Ulthera is the cosmetic system on which most skin-tightening studies have been done, according to the 2020 study's background [2].

In the 2015 study, two handpieces with focal depths of 3 mm and 4.5 mm were used for three to five passes, spaced 1 to 2 mm apart [1]. Results are assessed weeks to months later, since the proposed mechanism is new collagen formation after thermal injury [1].

Non-surgical tightening of the jawline and neck is part of the wider interest in sharper lower-face definition, and focused ultrasound sits among energy-based options beside radiofrequency and threads; the registered trial NCT04157218 planned to compare thread lifting with microfocused ultrasound for face tightening in 45 participants [4]. Doublo itself is a clinic-based device from HIRONIC of Seongnam, Korea, so access is through providers rather than home use [1]. Results are described as modest and suited to mild sagging, in line with the authors' selection of patients with minor sagging and no volume loss [2].

At two months in the 2015 study, subjective improvement was 63.6% and objective improvement was 72.7%. Staining of biopsies showed increased collagen fibres in the lower dermis and between fat layers, and the authors called the technique effective and safe in this small group of Asian patients [1].

The 2020 study had 43 patients with neck and lower-face laxity. Two independent dermatologists scored response on a 0 to 5 scale, where 0 meant exacerbation and 5 meant 75 to 100 percent improvement, and sagging, volume loss, satisfaction and tolerance were recorded. The abstract reports that nine subjects (52.9 percent) showed some improvement, which implies a smaller analysed group than the 43 treated, and that erythema and edema were acute and transient. The authors concluded that ultrasound appears to be a safe modality for facial skin tightening in selected patients with minor sagging and no volume discrepancy, and described the technology as having a good safety profile but limited efficacy [2]. The abstract gives no follow-up schedule.

The 2015 study, with 11 patients and two months of follow-up, is described by its design as preliminary, and its authors framed it as an option for Asian patients [1]. Neither study includes a control group.

Two published studies examine Doublo. The 2015 study had 11 patients with biopsies and blinded photographic assessment [1]. The 2020 prospective study included 43 patients with neck and lower-face laxity [2]. A registered trial (NCT04157218, status unknown) planned to compare thread lifting and microfocused ultrasound for face tightening in 45 participants [4].

card.summary: Korean HIFU skin-tightening device with two small published studies in Asian patients.
card.note: Evidence is limited to two small studies.

quick.overview:
Doublo is a Korean-made focused-ultrasound device used to tighten facial and neck skin.

Two small studies (11 and 43 patients) have been published; one authors' group described the technology as safe but of limited efficacy.
quick.mechanism: Focused ultrasound creates heat at various depths below the skin surface while sparing the surface layer.
quick.risks: The 2020 study describes IFUS as having a good safety profile; details beyond that were not available in the reviewed sources.
